chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
The Qa'im will rise and there is no allegiance (bay'ah) on his neck for anyone.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (The Rising One), a title for Imam al-Mahdi
key_terms.بَيْعَةٌ: Allegiance or pledge of loyalty, typically to a ruler
key_terms.لِأَحَدٍ: For anyone (indicating no prior submission to previous authorities)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the Qa'im has no bay'ah on his neck?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith highlights the political independence of Imam al-Mahdi upon his reappearance, asserting that his authority is not contingent upon prior allegiance to the Umayyad or Abbasid caliphs. This distinction serves to validate his divine mandate (Hujjiyyah) against the prevailing claims of legitimacy by contemporary rulers, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the Imam's inherent right to rule.
